title: Extend scrape to EPYC server platforms (SP3/SP5/SP6)
description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Scrapers today cover only consumer Ryzen (AM4/AM5). EPYC server platforms are out of reach via the same channels because BIOS distribution flows through system OEMs and AMD reference releases instead of motherboard vendors. We do care about server firmware (often the most interesting target — Pluton-HSP, server-side bootloaders, SEV apps), so this is on the roadmap.

Sockets to cover (descending priority by hardware availability):
- SP5 — Genoa / Bergamo / Siena / Turin (zen4 / zen5 server)
- SP3 — Naples / Rome / Milan (zen1 / zen2 / zen3 server)
- SP6 — Siena (zen4c)
- SH5 — Threadripper / Threadripper Pro overlap with EPYC SoC

Likely sources to evaluate:
- AMD reference BIOS releases (developer.amd.com / AMD AGESA drops)
- Supermicro, Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Gigabyte server line, Asus server line — each has its own download portal
- Wayback Machine CDX for the equivalent vendor CDNs (already a working pattern for ASRock/MSI)
- Coreboot / OpenSIL trees that ship reference firmware

Schema impact: minimal. images.socket already accepts free text — just allow SP3/SP5/SP6/SH5 alongside AM4/AM5. Optionally add a derived 'platform' column ('Ryzen' | 'EPYC' | 'Threadripper') to make group-by queries easier.

Until this lands, README documents EPYC as a known limitation. Manual ingest of EPYC ROMs already works; only auto-scraping is missing.

Depends on / informed by L2 (survey of other AMD BIOS scrapers — server scrapers may already exist).
